title: REF-QUAL-KIMI-JSON: the matched-protocol re-solve: is a better reference buyable, and is Kimi it? (569 reasoning calls under the incumbent's JSON answer-only protocol at a 32,768-token cap)
question: After two instrument failures (8,192 cap; an unmatched CoT prompt), solve Kimi-K2.6 under the incumbent's exact protocol (judge_solve_map.SYSTEM, user_prompt, parse_answer) with a 32,768-token cap in its own cache: (1) beat 0.726 on the discriminating subset by >= 3pp; (3) no frontier contestant gains > 3pp of agreement; (4) NEW: non-termination on the discriminating subset <= 5%, or the candidate fails on deployability whatever its accuracy.

registration.heading: ## Registered 2026-09-15 (before any run) — six tests from the big picture after the review. Standing rules from the review apply to all six: every wrong-direction count carries its McNemar-established count on the anchor's judged questions; UNDETERMINED is a registered outcome; the key denominator is named; nulls preserve what the question conditions on; the data object is checked before strata are read into it.
outcome_heading: L3510: - **REF-QUAL-KIMI-JSON (2026-09-15, 569 calls, the matched-protocol re-solve): DO NOT PROMOTE - gates (3) and (4) FAIL. And the accuracy underneath is the strongest a candidate reference has shown, which is the finding for the paper: a better reference EXISTS; this one is not deployable and would leak.**

sentence_of_record: REF-QUAL-KIMI-JSON (2026-09-15, 569 calls, the matched-protocol re-solve): DO NOT PROMOTE; gates (3) and (4) FAIL. The guard refused the gate correctly: 20 of 294 discriminating answers (6.8%) hit the cap, all 'length'; beneath it the strongest reference gain measured on this subset (terminated paired 0.821 vs 0.737; truncation-as-wrong 0.765 vs 0.724, +4.1pp), recorded as a non-gate number. Gate (3) FAILS at +0.071 on gemini: a more accurate reference agrees more with the most accurate contestant BY CONSTRUCTION (DECOMP's leakage), so (3) is coupled to what (1) rewards. Gate (4) FAILS at 6.8%. The falsifier fires; the Kimi line is closed. What stands: a better reference exists in principle, fails on exactly the two axes the programme predicted, and a future leakage gate should condition agreement on correctness.

plain_description.what: The test re-solved 569 questions with the Kimi model under exactly the same answer protocol as the current reference model. It checked whether Kimi would be a better reference for the judge, applying gates on accuracy, bias toward one contestant, and failure to finish answers.
plain_description.why: A more accurate reference answer is the biggest lever on judge accuracy, so a better reference was worth looking for.
plain_description.information: Passing would mean promoting Kimi as the reference. Failing shows which obstacles block a better reference. Result: done. Not promoted: two gates failed. First, Kimi is more accurate (about +4 points), but 6.8% of its answers hit the length limit, above the 5% allowed. Second, it failed the bias gate: it agrees more with the strongest contestant, which follows from being more accurate. The Kimi line is closed. A future bias check should take correctness into account. Later ruled history rather than evidence, because it ran on the older question pool.
